reduce: block-read lse
note: scalar lse loads LOOK dominant but the slice is cached; reduce is partial-buffer bandwidth bound

change: qq_bias: build mask per t, not per row
note: mask depends only on query_spec; 8 calls produced 2 distinct masks. 96/96 bit-identical.

change: all-dummy threads take mask fast path
note: padded thread was COSTLIER than a real one; dummy rows are discarded by row_valid anyway

change: TILE_Q rung table {16,8,6}
note: cost is set by how 8 marshal chunks divide: thr 1..8 -> .968/.590/.523/.555/.713/.890/.984/.820 (NON-monotonic)

change: software-pipeline marshal vs consume (SLM_SLOTS=2)
note: barrier ablation promised 8.9% but only ~1/3 survives: interleaving keeps both working sets live. Sign depends on chunks-per-thread, which is why the old A/B never converged.

change: fp16 partition partials
numbers: ~7.5% of the pair; error = 1 fp16 ulp (0.61x max / 1.00x rms of the existing final rounding)
note: declined for accuracy exposure: absolute error does not shrink when the cross-partition sum cancels. lse MUST stay f32 regardless.

change: DEQUANT_MAD (fold sub+mul into mad)
note: a consistent WIN, retiring the older '+1 to +3%' verdict as a rig artifact -- but not worth 2x typical error for 0.9% at q=16

change: MARSHAL_TG < WG_THREADS (more chunks/thread for ILP)
note: maximum marshal parallelism wins; the original note in the kernel was right

change: runtime TILE_Q (drop the rung machinery)
note: loses compile-time specialisation. Prototype exists. Would delete pick_small_q_rung entirely if ever worth it.

change: KV_PARTITION_SIZE=640
numbers: worst +168% / mean +40% vs per-case best; 3.3x regression at past=512
note: tuned at 15k only. Partition sets the WG count, so a big partition starves short contexts (1 partition = 8 WGs of 3 threads). 128:+44/+17  256:+47/+21  384:+118/+23

change: REDUCE_SPLIT_SIZE=128
numbers: only ~4% of reduce; breaks the PLUGIN (garbage output, 0 accepted tokens)
note: sandbox passes 240/240 at 128 on host AND container, at 192 and 256 GRF. Stock kernel fails too, so not the change. Suspect buffer alignment: 128-wide split makes the block read 512 B. Confirm SMALL_Q_PARTITIONOUT alignment before retrying.

change: ABLATE_NO_DPAS probe
note: replacement (half->float vector adds) costs more than the DPAS and breaks the accumulator chain. DPAS share of this kernel is STILL UNMEASURED.

change: runtime KV_PARTITION_SIZE
note: only the 3 prologue lookaside vectors need a compile-time extent; size them at MAX and everything else follows a scalar. Reuses the spare q_len_unused arg, no ABI change. Unlocks per-inference partition choice (mean +21% currently given up).

change: multi-sequence coverage for the small-q path
note: ALL small-q sandbox tests are single-sequence (subsequence_begins=[0,q_len]); test_pa_multiseq.py does not touch small-q. Mechanism looks right: nparts is sized from the batch max and each WG early-outs on its own seq_kv_partition_num (which does use the runtime partition, verified). But nothing verifies it, and that covers the rung table, the qq_bias fix and the all-dummy fast path too. Separately, pick_small_q_partition is calibrated at tile_count=1: with N sequences the tile axis supplies N x the parallelism for free, so the rule picks too-SMALL a partition and pays needless partial traffic. Correct but suboptimal. Proper rule should target total threads = tile_count * kv_heads * chunks_per_kv * nparts * wg_threads.

change: wider global 2D block load (MARSHAL_LOAD_W)
note: Fat loads ARE better per thread (at 4 threads 0.929 vs 0.999 thin; at 2, 1.223 vs 1.362) so the thin-message diagnosis was right. But MARSHAL_CHUNKS_C=8 means W>1 costs threads, and the marshal is thread-parallelism limited. Structurally closed at head_size=128: W>1 and 8 marshal threads are mutually exclusive.

change: raise occupancy by cutting per-thread live state
numbers: no GRF spill at 160/192/256; asm near-identical (14879/14870/14836 lines, 577 sends); 160 measured SLOWER (0.919 vs 0.819)
note: Only flag-register spills exist (rf=f1 predicates), never GRF. So there is no spill headroom to reclaim, AND more resident threads measured worse -- the signature of a bandwidth-bound kernel where extra concurrency only adds contention. Kills the whole 'cut Omat to raise occupancy' line.

change: roofline for q_len=16 @15k
numbers: floor 0.35 ms (46 MB / 132 GB/s measured); compute 0.20 ms (4.03 GFLOP / 19.93 TFLOPS measured); actual 0.845 -> gap 2.4x
note: Both roofs now MEASURED, not inferred (dram_bw.py, dpas_peak.py). Compute is only 57% of the memory floor so it should hide underneath, but the terms add instead. ~34% of the traffic (13.1 MB written + 13.1 MB read) is the split-K partial buffer, i.e. an algorithm artifact, not compulsory.

change: KV_PARTITION_SIZE beyond 640
note: Raising SMALL_Q_PARTITION_MAX itself is FREE (part=640 measures 0.919 at MAX=640 vs 0.909 at MAX=1280) -- the extra 4.5 GRF costs nothing, consistent with there being no GRF spill. But partitions past 640 lose parallelism faster than they save partial traffic: WGs = kv_heads * nparts, so 1280 gives 104 WGs against 640's 200. The 640 cap was right for the reason it was set, not by luck.

change: PIPELINE_MARSHAL (SLM double-buffer) gated per-rung instead of globally
shape: cmpr=2 block=256 past=15360, q=16 part 640/512, q=6 part 640
note: The ledger 3.2% win is at part 512, which pick_small_q_partition never selects (it picks 128/256/384/640). At 640 pipelining is neutral-to-worse, so per-rung gating buys nothing unless the partition rule changes.

change: harness fix: lru_cache on _create_kernels_ov_exp ignored env-derived build flags
numbers: in-process A/B of a flag known to cost 45% reported +0.0%
note: OV_EXP_EXTRA_FLAGS / OV_EXP_REG_FILE_SIZE were read inside the cached function so they were not in the cache key; the second arm got the first arm kernel. Now explicit params, maxsize 8->32. Prior sweeps used one process per value so the per-process cache never aliased -- no earlier finding is invalidated.

change: SPLIT_BARRIER: split the pre-marshal barrier into cm_sbarrier arrive/wait, wait pushed past the K load+dequant+transpose to just before the first SLM write
shape: cmpr=2 block=256, q=16 at the (context,partition) pairs the rule produces
note: Correct (29/29 tile_q=16 cases). Sign negative in 7/7 measurements so the effect is probably real but ~0.5%, a tenth of the 8.9% lockstep it targets. Hypothesis that KV_PREFETCH_DIST=1 made it redundant was REFUTED: with prefetch off it gets worse (0.923->0.971). q=16 only by construction (needs MARSHAL_CPT==1, enforced by #error). Kept in tree at default 0.

change: measured the roof for the kernel ACCESS PATTERN (paged 2D block 16x16 @pitch 128) instead of comparing against the sequential-stream roof
shape: 512 MiB working set, 512 groups x 8 threads, microbench/kv_pattern_bw.py
numbers: stream 128.4 GB/s; 2d-block seq pf0 79.6; paged pf0 78.2; seq pf1 101.5; paged pf1 106.0. Kernel achieves 95-101 GB/s = 95-100% of its pattern roof.
note: The 2.4x whole-kernel gap was computed against 132 GB/s streaming, which this pattern cannot reach. KV read is DONE. Paging indirection is free (shuffled == identity); the 22% deficit vs streaming is the 16B tile width, and prefetch recovers +28% of it. Revised floor ~0.42ms vs 0.845 actual, and all of the remainder is non-memory (dequant/softmax/barrier/SLM). Explains why three separate attacks on the barrier lockstep all came back empty: they were hiding work behind a stream already prefetched clear.

change: MARSHAL_HOIST_V=2: hoist V raw load into the K chunk loop so both 2D-block loads are outstanding at once; V dequant and V prefetch stay put
shape: cmpr=2 block=256, q=16 at the (context,partition) pairs the rule produces, 20 rounds
note: Predicted by microbench/kv_pattern_bw.py: two concurrent 2D-block streams hit 133 GB/s vs 109 for one. Two failed intermediates matter: moving only the PREFETCH (MARSHAL_PREFETCH_BOTH) loses 3.8-5.6% by aging Vs line out of L1 (consistent with the KV_PREFETCH_DIST 2/4 losses), and moving load+prefetch together nets ~0 because the effects cancel. Only separating them wins. Costs 2 GRF at 243/256, no spill. q=16 only: MARSHAL_CPT must be 1.

change: MARSHAL_PREFETCH_BOTH: issue Vs prefetch in the K loop, keeping Vs load in place
shape: cmpr=2 block=256, q=16 and q=6, 10 rounds
note: Zero register cost but loses everywhere. Reproduces only half the microbench configuration: the prefetches become concurrent while Vs load still sits behind the whole K body, so Vs prefetch is effectively at a longer distance and its line ages out of L1. Superseded by MARSHAL_HOIST_V=2.

change: qq_bias cost re-measured on the current plugin kernel (post MARSHAL_HOIST_V), q_len=16
shape: q_len=16, past=15360, part=640, block=256, cmpr=2, reg=192 (qq_probe.py QQ_RTPART=1)
note: Resolves why OV end-to-end never gets under 0.8ms even after MARSHAL_HOIST_V: the sandbox kernel pa_small_q_ov_exp.cm has ZERO qq_bias code (grep count 0), so every sandbox/full-matrix number this session excludes it entirely. Real EAGLE3 tree decoding always runs HAS_QQ_BIAS=1. Also surfaced a second, smaller, unexplained gap: sandbox 0.757ms vs plugin HAS_QQ_BIAS=0 0.840ms (~10%) that is not qq_bias and is not yet root-caused. The older ledger entry (q6, +5.9%) is not comparable -- mask is spec x spec so q16 (256 elements) costs far more than q6 (36).

change: qq_bias skip-guard: add symmetric upper bound so tiles entirely past the spec window are also skipped, not just tiles entirely before it
shape: q_len in {4,6,8,16}, cmpr in {1,2}, block in {16,256}, past_len in {15360(=24x640), 3100, 8100, 700, 1} (boundary-aligned and mid-partition), qq_probe.py / qq_boundary_equiv.py
numbers: qq_bias cost 0.089ms/+10.6% -> 0.010-0.013ms/+1.2-1.5% at q_len=16 past=15360. Main kernel with HAS_QQ_BIAS=1: 0.929ms -> ~0.845ms.
note: Root cause: since qq_bias_spec_num <= REG_N (16), at most one online tile per partition can ever straddle the spec window, but the old guard (kv_gs+blk_lo+REG_N <= past_q_lens) only excluded tiles before the window -- every tile from the window to the end of the partition (up to ~39 of 40 at KV_PARTITION_SIZE=640) still ran the full per-t build_qq_bias_tree_mask_row loop only to have its inner range check discard every lane. Fix adds kv_gs+blk_lo >= past_q_lens+qq_bias_spec_num to the same continue. Verified 400/400 bit-identical (qq_boundary_equiv.py) across 4 q_len x 2 cmpr x 2 block x 5 past_len x 5 mask patterns, 3 of which measurably change the result. Discovered while investigating why OV end-to-end never got under 0.8ms even after MARSHAL_HOIST_V -- see the prior open entry.

change: root cause of the sandbox-vs-plugin 9-10% gap found: runtime kv_partition_size scalar (kv_part_steps) vs sandbox compile-time KV_PARTITION_STEP_NUM constant
shape: q_len=16, cmpr=2, block=256, HAS_QQ_BIAS=0, three partition sizes
numbers: part=640/past=16000: 0.874->0.805ms (-7.9%); part=384/past=2048: 0.151->0.136ms (-9.9%); part=128/past=512: 0.045->0.042ms (-6.7%), forcing kv_part_steps to a compile-time constant via FORCE_CONST_PART_STEPS in qq_probe
note: pick_small_q_partition picks the right VALUE at runtime but the plugin passes it as a scalar arg rather than selecting a separately-compiled variant, so kv_part_steps (6 use sites: loop trip counts and per-tile guards) can never be constant-folded. This is exactly the fix paged_attention_gen.hpp already proposed in its own comment (compile partition variants like SMALL_Q_EXTRA_RUNG_TILE_Q does for TILE_Q) but the implementation took the scalar-argument shortcut instead. Fix: extend the rung mechanism to cover kv_partition_size the same way it covers TILE_Q, so pick_small_q_partition selects a compiled kernel instead of a scalar. Not yet implemented -- this closes the sandbox-vs-plugin discrepancy investigation but the fix itself is new work.

change: multi-sequence correctness coverage added for the small-q kernel (test_pa_small_q_multiseq.py)
shape: uniform-past 3-seq, heterogeneous-past 4-seq (seq_kv_partition_num 1..24 against one batch kv_partition_num), multi-tile-per-seq, cmpr x block_size cross, order-independence
numbers: 8/8 new tests pass; 123/123 with the existing correctness suite
note: Closes the previously-open multi-sequence gap: the batching mechanism (per-WG seq_kv_partition_num early-out against a batch-max kv_partition_num GWS dim, and the finalize kernel routing each tile through subsequence_begins[orig_seq_idx]) was correct by inspection but never exercised. Verified the checks have teeth via mutation: forcing all sequences past_lens to sequence 0s value makes the correctness check fail as expected (not vacuously passing). Order-independence test needed a fix to the input builder itself: a single global RNG consumed in list order made a sequences random data depend on which OTHER sequences preceded it in the batch; switched to a per-sequence torch.Generator seeded by (seed, past_len, q_len). Still open: pick_small_q_partition sizing for multi-sequence batches (recorded separately) -- this entry is correctness only, not partition-size tuning.

change: added KernelSpec.reference (TorchReference): independent SDPA ground truth via test_pa_small_q._build_inputs, combine() reimplements the logsumexp partition merge in torch
shape: ckh equiv pa_small_q, q_len in {4,6}, past_len in {512,2048,8000}, cmpr=2, block=256
numbers: max_abs_diff 2.4e-5 to 8e-5 across shapes, well within tol=(5e-2,5e-2). Mutation test: replacing the correct logsumexp-weighted merge with an unweighted mean raises max_abs_diff to 0.11 and flips PASS to FAIL.
note: This is the first ckh equiv reference wired up. combine() is independent of the reduce KERNEL -- comparing against a reimplementation of the very thing under test would prove nothing. See kernels/pa_small_q.py.

change: new spec kernels/pa_small_q_vs_baseline.py: pa_small_q_ov.cm (TILE_Q=2 fixed, lws=[1,1,1], no cooperative marshalling) wired up as a KernelReference baseline for pa_small_q_ov_exp.cm
shape: ckh equiv pa_small_q_vs_baseline, q_len in {4,6}, past_len in {512,2048,8000}, partition=256, cmpr=2, block=256
numbers: max_abs_diff 3.3e-5 to 8.0e-5 on partition_out/lse across 6 shapes, tol tightened to (1e-3,1e-3) accordingly. Mutation test: forcing the baseline to see a wrong constant past_lens raises max_abs_diff to 3e38 (an unmasked -inf lse) and flips PASS to FAIL.
